paper.title: OMG: Omni-Modal Motion Generation for Generalist Humanoid Control

decision_relevance.why_admitted: OMG directly studies an upstream, multimodally steerable reference generator whose output is executed by a pre-existing downstream humanoid tracker. Its explicit condition interfaces, guidance weights, temporal contract, root-frame convention, and target-versus-executed metrics make it a concrete candidate mechanism for Sam's reference-composition knob under a frozen tracker.
not_evidence_for: An outer-loop agent that revises an oracle from evaluation metrics
OGMP state-machine, predicate, or branching-oracle execution
Quantitative success of zero-shot text-plus-audio composition
Dynamic feasibility or safety of arbitrary generated references
A fully fixed trainer when adapting OMG-DiT to a new modality
Apple-Silicon latency matching the reported NVIDIA deployment

mechanisms.name: Generator-tracker hierarchy
mechanisms.description: A high-level generator predicts future whole-body reference observations from recent history and external conditions; a pre-existing HoloMotion tracker maps those references to executable Unitree G1 actions.

mechanisms.name: Root-canonical G1 motion contract
mechanisms.description: Each model frame is a 125D G1 feature vector canonicalized to the last history frame's root position and yaw; outputs are decoded back to world-frame G1 states before tracking.

mechanisms.name: Shared diffusion motion prior
mechanisms.description: A DiT denoiser predicts a 60-frame clean future motion from a noisy future, ten history frames, and a subset of available conditions using an x-prediction objective.

mechanisms.name: Global cross-attention condition interface
mechanisms.description: Canonical motion-history tokens and frozen T5-Base language embeddings are projected into the hidden dimension and supplied as cross-attention context in every DiT block.

mechanisms.name: Frame-aligned FiLM condition interface
mechanisms.description: Audio and 22-joint human-reference features are aligned to future motion frames and injected through per-layer FiLM modulation with availability masks.

mechanisms.name: Modality-specific classifier-free guidance
mechanisms.description: At each denoising step, text, audio, and human-reference directions are formed relative to a null branch and combined with independent guidance scales, enabling explicit weighted composition of control signals.

mechanisms.name: Zero-initialized new-modality adapters
mechanisms.description: A new global condition can append context tokens, while a new frame-aligned condition can add FiLM or AdaLN-style adapters whose final linear layer is initialized to zero; the reported experiments then fully finetune the backbone.

mechanisms.name: Tracker-executed data filter
mechanisms.description: Retargeted trajectories are executed through the deployment tracker in MuJoCo and rejected for non-finite states, persistent falls, and, where strict feasibility is required, joint-limit violations.

mechanisms.name: Chunk-level temporal condition sequence
mechanisms.description: The official pipeline supports ordered text, audio, human-reference, text-plus-audio, and text-plus-human-reference chunks in synchronous or asynchronous generator-tracker execution modes.

failure_modes.name: Flat-ground data scope
failure_modes.description: The authors report that training data mainly cover flat-ground motions and that uneven or in-the-wild terrain remains challenging.

failure_modes.name: No execution-feedback adaptation
failure_modes.description: The work focuses on motion generation, does not jointly adapt generator and tracker, and leaves incorporation of execution feedback into generation for future work.

failure_modes.name: Over-guidance can worsen global tracking
failure_modes.description: In the human-reference sweep, raising guidance from 1.5 to 2.0 lowers root-relative MPJPE from 74.0 to 71.0 mm but worsens g-MPJPE from 218.9 to 343.9 mm.

failure_modes.name: Qualitative composition evidence
failure_modes.description: Zero-shot text-plus-audio composition is supported by qualitative figures and demonstrations, not by a dedicated quantitative composition benchmark.

failure_modes.name: G1 and HoloMotion coupling
failure_modes.description: Training targets, canonical features, output qpos, filters, and execution metrics are defined for Unitree G1 and the HoloMotion tracker; transfer to another embodiment or controller is untested here.

failure_modes.name: Public checkpoint path mismatch
failure_modes.description: At the pinned public revisions, the GitHub README links checkpoints/300m/sstep=055000.ckpt, while the Hugging Face tree and checksum manifest place the paper artifact under checkpoints/paper/300m/sstep=055000.ckpt.

evaluation.name: Generation-quality and execution-fidelity benchmark
evaluation.description: The evaluation reports modality-specific generation metrics separately from tracker-executed contact sliding, jerk, pose/velocity/acceleration errors, fall rate, and joint-limit violation rate.

evaluation.name: Human-reference retargeting benchmark
evaluation.description: OMG-DiT-XL reports 18.84 mm root-relative and 47.83 mm global target MPJPE, then 43.07 mm and 112.60 mm tracker-executed target errors, with 0.39% falls and 23.05% joint-limit violations.

evaluation.name: Text-conditioned benchmark
evaluation.description: OMG-DiT-XL reports the strongest tabled text-motion FID, Matching Score, and R-precision among compared methods, while some tracker-fidelity columns favor OMG-DiT-L or baselines.

evaluation.name: Audio-conditioned benchmark
evaluation.description: OMG-DiT improves tabled FID-k and FID-g over compared audio baselines but does not lead every beat-alignment, PFC, contact-slide, jerk, or tracking-fidelity metric.

evaluation.name: Few-shot and new-modality adaptation
evaluation.description: On held-out AMASS-CMU/WEIZMANN, OMG initialization outperforms same-architecture training from scratch at 1%, 10%, and 100% data for text and Pico-keypoint tasks.

evaluation.name: Human-reference CFG sweep
evaluation.description: Four human-reference guidance scales are compared across MPJPE, g-MPJPE, and rollout horizons, exposing a non-monotonic local-versus-global alignment tradeoff.

evaluation.name: Planner runtime benchmark
evaluation.description: A staged A800 benchmark measures PyTorch, compiled, ONNX, TensorRT, FP16, and cache optimizations for one 60-frame text-conditioned DiT-B plan.

evaluation.name: Perceptive-locomotion adaptation
evaluation.description: After 500 training steps on the stated visual task, pretrained initialization reaches 53 of 90 successes versus 44 of 90 from scratch under the paper's pelvis-in-target criterion.

evidence.locator: Metadata and submission history, lines 8-27; v1 submitted 2026-06-09
evidence.claim: The active primary record is arXiv:2606.10340v1 by eight listed authors, with arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2606.10340.

evidence.locator: Sec. 3.1, Problem Formulation, generator-tracker factorization
evidence.claim: OMG factorizes control into a high-level future-reference generator and a low-level tracker and uses pre-existing HoloMotion as the tracker.

evidence.locator: Sec. 3.2; appendix Details of OMG-DiT, Motion Representation, Denoising Backbone, Sampling, Model Scales, and Training Hyperparameters
evidence.claim: The source specifies the 125D canonical G1 representation, 10-frame history, 60-frame horizon, DiT variants, diffusion objective, DDIM sampler, and training settings.

evidence.locator: Sec. 3.3; appendix Omni-Modal Condition Encoders and Adapting to New Modalities
evidence.claim: Language and history use cross-attention; 35D audio and 66D human reference use frame-wise FiLM; modality dropout and zero-initialized new adapters are specified.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Classifier-Free Guidance and Composition, modality-specific equation and practical scales
evidence.claim: Null-relative text, audio, and human-reference guidance directions can be added with separate weights; reported defaults are 3.0, 1.5, and 2.0 for the respective uses.

evidence.locator: Sec. 2; appendix Details on OMG-Data, Dataset Composition and Simulation-in-the-Loop Filtering
evidence.claim: OMG-Data contains 1174.66 processed hours at 30 Hz, and tracker-executed MuJoCo rollouts are screened using explicit fall and joint-limit criteria.

evidence.locator: Sec. 4.1; appendix Evaluation Protocols and Shared Evaluation Metrics
evidence.claim: The benchmark separates modality-specific target-generation quality from tracker-executed physical and failure metrics and states the validation sample counts.

evidence.locator: Table titled Human-reference-conditioned motion benchmark, OMG-DiT-L and OMG-DiT-XL rows
evidence.claim: The paper reports target-motion, tracker-executed, fall, and joint-limit values for human-reference-conditioned OMG variants.

evidence.locator: Table titled Text-conditioned motion benchmark, all rows
evidence.claim: The text benchmark reports generation and tracker-execution metrics for OMG-DiT-L, OMG-DiT-XL, and five baseline variants.

evidence.locator: Table titled Audio-conditioned motion benchmark, all rows
evidence.claim: The audio benchmark reports alignment, distribution, physical, tracker-fidelity, fall, and joint-limit metrics for OMG and baselines.

evidence.locator: Sec. 4.3, paired Text-to-Motion Finetuning and Pico Keypoint-Based Teleoperation tables
evidence.claim: Pretrained OMG initialization outperforms same-architecture scratch training across reported data fractions for held-out text and Pico tasks.

evidence.locator: Sec. 4.4, Zero-shot Compositionality; appendix qualitative visualization and Text-audio CFG sweep figure
evidence.claim: The zero-shot text-plus-audio composition claim is illustrated qualitatively; no dedicated quantitative composition table is reported.

evidence.locator: Limitations
evidence.claim: The authors identify flat-ground data, lack of joint generator-tracker adaptation, and lack of execution feedback in generation as limitations or future directions.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Analysis on Classifier-Free Guidance, Human-reference CFG sweep table
evidence.claim: Moderate guidance improves alignment, but root-relative and global MPJPE respond differently and overly strong guidance can hurt performance.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Runtime Acceleration Analysis table
evidence.claim: TensorRT FP16 plus DiT caching generates a 60-frame DiT-B text-conditioned plan in 51.7 plus or minus 1.5 milliseconds on one A800 in five steady-state runs.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Adaptation to New Modalities: Perceptive Locomotion
evidence.claim: At 500 steps, pretrained initialization succeeds in 53 of 90 held-out target rollouts versus 44 of 90 from scratch under the stated success rule.

evidence.locator: Lines 9-35 and 52-85, pipeline modes, condition sequence, sync and async execution
evidence.claim: The official code snapshot exposes chunk-level multimodal condition sequences and separate diffusion-only, tracker-only, synchronous, asynchronous, and offline-track modes.
